identity.title: CoEvol-NO: State and Coordinate Co-Evolution with an Error-Driven Predictor-Corrector Paradigm for Neural Operator Transformer

problem.claim: Long-sequence modeling remains a challenge in neural operator learning.

gap.claim: Existing methods are characterized as treating latent states as transient or decoupled rather than jointly and bidirectionally updating them with the mesh sequence.

contributions.claim: Introduces CoEvol-NO, a persistent-state co-evolutionary framework that jointly and bidirectionally updates latent state and mesh sequence.
Formulates layer-wise state evolution as a predictor-corrector process with error-driven refinement of the persistent state.
Analyzes direct substitution and residual update as first-order approximations of error-driven correction under different loss assumptions, and proves strict linear time complexity for CoEvol-NO.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CoEvol-NO through a persistent state and joint bidirectional co-evolution of state and mesh sequence.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a theoretical proof of strict linear time complexity.
The authors report that experiments on five standard benchmarks and two large-scale industrial design tasks consistently achieve state-of-the-art performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-sequence modeling is identified as an ongoing challenge for neural operator learning.
CoEvol-NO introduces a persistent latent state and co-evolves it with the mesh sequence in both directions.
Layer-wise evolution follows a predictor-corrector process: prediction proposes a target, then error-driven correction refines the persistent state.
The analysis relates direct substitution and residual updates to first-order approximations under differing loss assumptions.
The authors report strict linear complexity and SOTA performance across seven evaluation settings spanning benchmarks and industrial design tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a persistent-state design to a predictor-corrector mechanism and interprets existing update paradigms as approximations under explicit loss assumptions.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim becomes more informative when its architectural choice, operational update rule, and relation to prior paradigms are presented together.
lessons.application: When proposing an iterative architecture, define the persistent quantity, state the update sequence, and map simpler baselines to approximations under named assumptions.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the method has no iterative state or when such approximation relationships have not been theoretically established.

unknowns: The specific loss assumptions behind the first-order-approximation claim are not given.
The setup and proof conditions for strict linear complexity are unspecified.
Benchmark names, baselines, metrics, and numerical margins for the reported SOTA results are absent.
